Thank you, Mr. Chair, ladies and members of committee. My name is Sarah King, housing and homelessness manager for the City of Saskatoon. I'll be presenting this report before you today regarding the proposed affordable housing property tax abatements for 2026.

The purpose of this report is to request approval of a five year incremental property tax abatements for nine affordable housing developments that would support the creation of 210 new affordable rental units in Saskatoon.

In advance and advance the City's affordable housing commitments under the Housing Accelerator Fund. The total estimated value of the proposed abatements is approximately 1.65 million over a five year period, including municipal library and education property taxes.

Council policies see zero nine zero zero two allows the City to provide property tax abatements for eligible affordable housing developments under this policy council may approve an incremental property tax abatement of up to five years for the affordable residential component of an eligible project.

These applications were submitted and reviewed under the previous incentive policy. As a result administration in consultation with the solicitor's office is recommending that these projects continue to be considered under the eligibility requirements and incentive structure that were in place when these applications were made this provides consistency and procedural fairness for applicants whose projects were advanced based on the existing program.
Applications will be considered under the city's new development incentives framework that recently went into effect following last week's council meeting.
In terms of the half targets under the city's Housing Accelerator Fund agreement Saskatoon must achieve a target of 733 new affordable housing units with building permits issued by December 31 2026.
As of July 2026 479 affordable units had received building permits and recounted towards this target leaving 254 units remaining to meet our goal.

The nine developments in this report include 210 new affordable rental units of these 44 have already been counted towards the half target will 166 represent additional eligible units to be counted if approved.

If all the proposed projects proceed as proposed the city's total would increase from 479 to 645 affordable units leaving 88 additional units remaining to meet the affordable housing target by the end of 2026.
The city is used housing accelerator fund funding to provide capital grants for a number of affordable housing projects over the last few years.
All available capital grant funding through that program has now been committed.
As a result 86 of the 210 affordable units included in this report are proposed to receive a property tax abatement without an accompanying capital grant.

Projects receiving only a property tax abatement will be required to remain affordable for at least 10 years projects that also receive a capital grant or subject to the 20 year affordability commitment.

All supported developments must enter into illegal agreements with the city and these agreements established the applicable affordability period and require ongoing monitoring and annual reporting to confirm that these units continue to meet our requirements.

In terms of financial implications the total estimated value as I mentioned is approximately 1.65 million of this amount approximately 1.1 million represents four gone city and library property tax revenue over the five year period.
Incremental tax abatements are treated as four gone revenue and do not require a direct funding source.
The estimates are based on 2026 tax rates.
The final abatements will be calculated using the actual assessed values following completion and final inspection of each development.
The amounts may also change based on modifications to project design or future mill rated adjustments.
Provincial approval is required when the estimated education property tax abatement for an individual project is greater than 25,000 per year.
The developments at 1,1011 street and 902 to 912 third avenue north are expected to exceed this threshold.
Therefore, if approved corporate revenue will submit applications to the province requesting approval of the education property tax portion of the abatements for those two projects.
In summary, the recommendations would support 9 housing developments 210 affordable rental units, 166 additional units to be counted towards the housing accelerator fund target.
A combined total of 1,042 new residential units between market and affordable across the developments and continued progress towards increasing the supply of affordable housing in Saskatoon.

Community safety and well-being framework update.
That's a good morning, Mr. Chair.
Let's say Anderson director planning and development again.
So just today's report is to provide an update for you and some background regarding the progress in developing our community safety and well-being framework for the city of Saskatoon.

Community safety and well-being is commonly understood as the ideal state of a sustainable community where everyone is safe has a sense of belonging has opportunities to participate and can meet their needs for education, healthcare, food, housing income and social and cultural expression.
CSWB plans across the country typically include four areas, which are social development, prevention, risk intervention and incident response.

And as we all know, Saskatoon and many other North American cities have been experiencing the interconnected challenges related to housing affordability, homelessness poverty, mental health and substance use and growing demand for incident response.
However, focusing only on incident response doesn't consider ways to prevent or intervene earlier, nor does it address the root causes of the social challenges that we're seeing in our cities.
So CSWB plans are intended to look at the other facets that are more upstream, so that's social development, prevention and inter risk intervention, but in a coordinated way.
So the community safety and well-being framework that we've been working on is intended to assist in building those preventative and community-based approaches.
As some further background for this update, this work emerged through a motion from City Council in June 2020 and requested administration to report on creation of a CSWB plan.
In January of 2021, we reported back with an outline of the rationale for developing the plan and a path to create one.
And that included an approach to phase-infunding to support plan development and implementation.
Edmund was directed to work with the council lead at the time to clarify scope and objectives and report on options to have the work completed.

During this period as we all know, we were dealing with the COVID pandemic, which brought forward numerous different and evolving social issues and impacted the discussions that we had around this issue.
There was a significant period of time spent to get agreement on how to approach the work and then to recruit for the appropriate position to support it.
That was in place. We then had to redirect our resources to work on an award of funding that we received under the building safer communities funding from the government of Canada.
So that definitely impacted our timeline for the development and delivery of this plan.
And which brings us here today to bring you this update to where we're outlining our current status and next steps.
So the plan itself is being developed over three phases. We're currently in phase two.
Phase one involved information gathering to better understand the similar work being done elsewhere, so it included a municipal scan and stakeholder consultations.
The phase also involved work by admin to secure additional resources through two research junction grants to support the knowledge gathering and development of evaluation and monitoring materials.
And we also received funding from the Ministry of Justice to undertake engagement and priority identification.
So we're now in phase two where the targeted community engagement is incurring and we have the assistance of a vagina-based consultant to do that work.
This engagement will help us identify priorities and keep performance indicators which will inform the final plan.
We've also been engaging within administration to share information and to better understand where the city has levers in our wheelhouse in our existing work.
And the potential future work that's already in our pathways that can contribute to this plan.
So for example are there ways that we can do service delivery to enhance equity or remove barriers to access, for example.
So those are some of the discussions that we're having internally.
In phase three we'll bring all of those components together to develop the overall framework which will include those monitoring and keep performance indicators and recommendations for further work.
So once developed with those components will all be brought forward to committee and council for your review and consideration for approval.
